deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page computes Gauss's lemniscate half-period, 1.3110287771... = ϖ/2. Gauss writes this constant as π, but here it means the lemniscate constant ϖ = 2.62205755..., not the circle constant. On this page 'sin', 'cos' and 'A.sin' mean the lemniscatic sine, cosine and arc-sine (sl, cl, arcsl). The page lists power series for sl, cl and for the entire functions P, Q, p, q with sl = P/Q and cl = p/q. It then states their convergence behaviour.

(1) Lemniscatic arc sine. arcsl x = ∫_0^x dt/√(1−t^4). Expand (1−t^4)^(−1/2) by the binomial series and integrate term by term:
arcsl x = Σ_n [(1·3···(2n−1))/(2·4···2n)] · x^(4n+1)/(4n+1)
= x + (1/2)(1/5)x^5 + (1·3/2·4)(1/9)x^9 + (1·3·5/2·4·6)(1/13)x^13 + (1·3·5·7/2·4·6·8)(1/17)x^17 + (1·3·5·7·9/2·4·6·8·10)(1/21)x^21 + ...
The x^17 and x^21 coefficients are written in the upper right.

(2) Lemniscatic sine by series reversion (my reading of the method: invert series (1), or equivalently solve sl'^2 = 1 − sl^4):
sl x = x − x^5/10 + x^9/120 − 11x^13/15600 + 211x^17/3536000 − 1607x^21/318240000 − ...
With factorial denominators this is x − 12x^5/5! + 3024x^9/9! − 4390848x^13/13! + 21224560896x^17/17! − 257991277243392x^21/21!.

(3) Numerator function P. In modern terms P is the Weierstrass sigma function σ(x; g2=4, g3=0).
P x = x − x^5/60 − x^9/10080 + 23x^13/259459200 + 107x^17/D
= x − 2x^5/5! − 36x^9/9! + 552x^13/13! + 5136x^17/17! (+ a struck-out term 5146848x^21/21!).
The numerators are 2^m·a_m with a_m = −1, −9, 69, 321, which are Weierstrass's sigma coefficients for g3 = 0.

(4) Denominator function Q, the co-sigma function σ_2 belonging to e = 0:
Q x = 1 + x^4/12 − x^8/10080 + 17x^12/19958400 + 283x^16/435891456000
= 1 + 2x^4/4! − 4x^8/8! + 408x^12/12! + 13584x^16/16!.
With these, sl = P/Q. Example check (mine): (x − x^5/60)(1 − x^4/12) gives x − x^5/10.

(5) Lemniscatic cosine:
cl x = 1 − x^2 + x^4/2 − 3x^6/10 + 7x^8/40 − 61x^10/600 + 71x^12/1200 − ...
In factorial form: 1 − 2x^2/2! + 12x^4/4! − 216x^6/6! + 7056x^8/8! − 368928x^10/10! + 28340928x^12/12!.

(6) The functions p and q (upper sign for p, lower for q), so that cl = p/q:
p, q = 1 ∓ x^2/2 − x^4/24 ∓ x^6/240 + 17x^8/40320 ∓ x^10/403200 + 37x^12/159667200 ...
These are the co-sigma functions for e = +1 (p) and e = −1 (q).
The numerator line 1, −1, −1, −3, +17, −9, +111 gives the coefficients times n!. For example 37·12!/159667200 = 111.
A struck-out x^12 attempt (…/…9600) is replaced by 37/159667200.
My check of the leading terms: with p = E − O and q = E + O, put u = O/E = x^2/2 + x^6/40 + ... Then cl = (1−u)/(1+u) = 1 − 2u + 2u^2 − 2u^3 ... = 1 − x^2 + x^4/2 − 3x^6/10 ✓.

(7) Latin text, translated: 'The formulas for P, Q, p, q continued to infinity converge faster than any given convergence (i.e., they are entire functions). But the formulas for sl x diverge if x > ϖ/√2, i.e. x^4 > ϖ^4/4; the formula for cl x diverges if x > ϖ.'

(8) Bottom scratch work.
- Differences of the P-numerators: 36 − 2 = 34, 552 + 36 = 588, 5136 − 552 = 4584. This looks like part of a recursion for the next coefficient.
- 3996 − 622 = 3374 = 14·241.
- 2911·4 = 11644; 11644·36 = 419184; 419184·2 = 838368.
- A faint pencil Q dP − P dQ, i.e. Q^2·d(sl).
- 1.707 ≈ 1 + 1/√2.
- Binomial coefficients 1/2, 3/8, 1/16, as in (1).
errors: The written denominator of the x^17 term of P (machine read 20748433056000; the image looks more like 20748433305600 = 7·17!/120) is inconsistent with Gauss's own correct factorial form 5136/17!. The correct value is 5136/17! = 107/7410154752000. Either this is a slip in reducing the fraction or a misreading.

Convergence claim for cl. Its poles nearest the origin are at ±iϖ/2, so the Maclaurin series of cl has radius ϖ/2, not ϖ. The written coefficients confirm this: the ratio (71/1200)/(61/600) ≈ 0.582 ≈ 4/ϖ^2. Gauss's statement 'diverges if x > ϖ' is true but far from sharp; the series already diverges for |x| > ϖ/2.
The claim for sl (radius ϖ/√2, from poles at (±1±i)ϖ/2) is correct.
The struck-out x^21 term of P (5146848/21!) is not verified here; Gauss himself cancelled it.

results.what: Binomial-series expansion of the lemniscatic arc-sine ∫dx/√(1−x^4)
results.modern_name: Maclaurin series of the lemniscate arcsine

results.what: Series reversion giving sl x and cl x to x^21 and x^12
results.modern_name: Maclaurin series of the lemniscatic sine and cosine (Dixon/Weierstrass-type coefficients)

results.what: Entire functions P, Q, p, q with sl = P/Q, cl = p/q, given as power series with factorial-normalised integer numerators
results.modern_name: Weierstrass sigma function σ(z;4,0) and co-sigma functions σ_i for the lemniscatic case

results.what: Radius of convergence of the sl series is ϖ/√2; the P, Q, p, q series converge everywhere
results.modern_name: Radius of convergence from the nearest poles; entire functions

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's lemniscatic functions P, Q (anticipating Weierstrass's σ) and their power series are published in Werke III and well discussed (Schlesinger, Markushevich). This page is a careful working sheet of known material. The radius-of-convergence remark via complex poles is a nice detail, but it is also known from his lemniscate notes.

checkable.asserts: arcsl series x + x^5/10 + 3x^9/72 + ... with coefficients (1·3···)/(2·4···)/(4n+1)
sl series satisfies sl'^2 = 1 - sl^4 through x^23 (result O(x**24))
sl = P/Q with these coefficients (result O(x**21)); fails if the x^17 term is 107/20748433056000 or 107/20748433305600
sigma identity p^2 = Q^2 - P^2 (σ_i^2 - σ_j^2 = (e_j - e_i)σ^2 with e = 1, 0, -1)
equals 0: the correct reduced x^17 coefficient of P

The denominator of the x^16 term of Q is 435891456000 (=16!/48), not 43589145600.
The denominator of the x^17 term of P is read as 20748433056000 but appears in the image as 20748433305600. Either way it disagrees with the correct 7410154752000.
The numerator sequence under p, q ends '+111' (= 37·12!/159667200), not '+14'.
The x^21 term 5146848/1…21 in the P line is struck out.
The crossed-out x^12 attempt in the p, q line reads approximately 251/…9600 with '21288' below it; it is replaced by 37/159667200.
